newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Chaplin son aims to build Swiss theme park.
newsitem.headline: Chaplin son aims to build Swiss theme park.

text.p: Eugene Chaplin, son of Charlie Chaplin, on Tuesday presented a 66 million Swiss franc ($45 million) project to build a multimedia theme park as a tribute to his famous father in Vevey, on the Swiss shores of Lake Geneva.
The "Time Machine" park, designed as the headquarters of a future network of 10 parks worldwide, could attract up to 500,000 visitors a year and boost the local economy, he added.

But Chaplin, who lives in the manor in nearby Corsier where his father spent his last 25 years, said he needed to raise roughly half the cost of the Swiss project, or 35 million Swiss francs ($20 million). The rest is to be financed by bank loans.

Organisers hope the first part of the Swiss park will be completed in 1999. Tourists could "visit the century" by viewing films in which Chaplin starred or directed at 10 cinemas which would be surrounded by educational and recreational activities.
Chaplin, born in 1889, starred in films including "The Kid", "Gold Rush", "Modern Times and "The Great Dictator".
"My father, Charlie Chaplin, was born 108 years ago tomorrow," Eugene Chaplin, 43, told a news conference in Vevey.
"The project which we present is dedicated to him: putting his work in the perspective of the 20th century.
Chaplin paid tribute to his father as "king of the screen whose humanist message is permanent through his films".

"My father lived 25 happy years in Vevey after coming to Switzerland in 1952 as a refugee from his American troubles," the son added, referring to his father as being among the Hollywood victims of the Communist "red scare".

Eugene Chaplin, fifth of eight children and sister of actress Geraldine Chaplin, noted that their father and mother were both buried in Corsier, in the hills above Vevey which overlook the Alps. "It is in their memory and honour that I conceived of the idea and developed the project 'Time Machine'.
